text_fidelity_a:
Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black I bought this for my husband who works outside and needed something to keep lunch plus multiple drinks cold all day.
PROS:
- Very large size - can hold 2 larger-sized gatorade drinks PLUS a 16.9 oz water bottle in the bottom compartment with an ice pack, and 2 sandwiches with 2 16.9 oz water bottles or more on top
- Very sturdy material - thick, tear resistant, very durable
- Comes with optional shoulder strap that fits perfectly in the front zippered compartment if you need to be hands free
- Looks more masculine than LL Bean-type of lunch bags so hubby actually uses it
- Front pocket is see through mesh and perfect to hold strap and a "tick key" tick remover for outdoor use
- At under 20 bucks, it's a real bargain! I bought an extra one and put it away for when this one bites the dust

CONS:
- Black color means it gets hot outdoors or in the car - especially if the sun hits it
- White interior shows every bit of dirt (although cleans up easily with a little baking soda-water paste on a sponge)
- Zippers are sturdy, but get "stuck" quite often
- Sides are soft so will the bag will sit lop-sided if unequal size items are placed in the bottom
- Triangular shaped top (with above mentioned soft sides) makes it so things on top are easily crushed
- Top handles are too small too fit a large sized wrist through so it must be carried by hand or shoulder strap

All in all a good lunch box for men (and women) who carry lots of food and drinks for lunch. I wish there were other color options- maybe an army green or tan- so it didn't get so hot in the sun. Would also be better if at least the bottom compartment had stiff sides. Also, a zippered pouch or compartment to hold a cold pack would be nice, so it didn't have to get mixed in with contents.

It's really hard to find a durable, masculine lunch box for guys who get dirty at work or work outdoors. I've looked for something decent for years and the selection is extremely limited. This fits the bill and is very reasonably priced. For under 20 bucks, you can't do any better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Minuteman 24-Hour Meal Kits 6-Pack It was a good learning experience trying this emergency food kit. Like with any preparedness item, it’s always smart to do a test run.

Everything is well organized in each individual 24-hour bag. I received 2 sets of 3 varying meal options. I sampled the Potato Chive, Chocolate Shake and Maple Oatmeal kit today. I love the canned water for easy opening and pouring for both drinking and food preparation.

-The powdered potatoes re-hydrated well and didn’t taste too bad. They are very palatable and the texture was fine.
-The oatmeal is VERY fragrant and tasted similar to a typical maple oatmeal packet from the grocery store. I liked it.
-The Protein shake tasted great, but it was problematic trying to get the powder to incorporate with the water. I tried both shaking and stirring, and I still couldn’t get the powder to mix very thoroughly. A blender bottle would be ideal, but obviously not feasible in an emergency.

These meal kits will certainly get you through a hard time, however, I feel the calorie count is a little low for the average person coming in around 1,000 calories for each kit. I think it would be great if another oatmeal packet was included or just something to help you hit about 1,200-1,300 calories for more satiety, especially in a time of need. This kit is still a great nutritional boost and highly valuable when you need it most.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Minuteman 24-Hour Meal Kits 6-Pack

All the reviews make it out to be something it most certainly is not. This is just a novelty kit with about $5 work of product (if that). Neat concept, poor execution. If you're looking for a survival kit with products that will actually help you survive something in real life...THIS IS NOT IT. Even as a themed novelty kit, this is junk. Save your money.

The most useful items are the anti-bacterial goop and the bandaids.

The card multi-tool could be useful, but ALL the edges are sharp and can easily break skin.

The "tactical knife" is a card-knife that can neither be properly locked open or properly locked closed. It struggled with cutting the plastic this survival kit came wrapped in.

The dust mask is unfinished on the edges. It can easily become unraveled and had lots of loose ends fresh out of the package.

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I wanted this specifically for its heart rate monitor and sleep monitor--something I can basically wear all the time. I specifically did not want a watch, because I wear a watch on my other arm. So this is just right for that. It's a tad bigger than it ideally could be. I hope future generations will slim down and maybe be more flexible and/or add more interesting sensors.

The sleep monitor seems to work okay. I previously had a Microsoft Band 2, and I feel it may have been better at that.

Since I don't use it as a watch, I like the option to turn off the feature to show time when lifting it up. So it stays black unless I really want it to show me something.

It lets you set like 7 alarms, which can repeat, and I use them to remind myself to drink water. So that's a nice plus.

It does seem a little slow to sync. Specifically, I often want to set a silent alarm right before bed, and it takes like a minute to sync. Then I set the alarm, and it takes several seconds to sync that. Then I can finally turn it on, and wait a few seconds to sync that. Pretty cumbersome. The Microsoft Band let you set it quickly on the Band, so it's much better in that way. (But my Band broke during normal use, and I went through a LOT of trouble to get Microsoft to replace it. A lot. Very bad customer service, so I can't recommend it.)

The battery life is good on this, but it's not great. That said, it's much easier to charge than the Blaze, which I also tried. I basically just charge it while I'm in the shower (a trick I learned for the Band), and that's more than enough. I have to say, I have almost gotten in the shower with it a few times. It is easy to forget you have it on!

So I think it's probably the best continuous HR and sleep monitor option that is specifically not trying to pretend to double as a smart watch.

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Resistance Band with Handles - Exercise Band Workout Cord with Comfort-Foam Handles for Fitness Strength Training | Ideal for Home Gym, Women, Men We have been working to improve and sustain our fitness, especially as we move through middle age. With a number of items we currently use (hand weights, bench w/weight bar, kettle bells, etc) we were looking at resistance bands to augment our options. We live in an apartment, so while there is the community workout room, in the age of Covid, we are avoiding that space. Two people working out at the same time can also take up too. much room and I sometimes workout late at night and do not want to make noise. So we took a chance on the FILA Accessories Resistance Band with Handles and we come away positive and happy with it.

This band is a great compliment to what we are already doing. I’ve been working on two areas: upper body/arms and lower body/legs/core. This supports that overall goal.

In my experience this heavy resistance has been great for my arms and challenges me. I do feel a solid burn and full on resistance.

My core does feel it unless I focus and make certain I’m getting it involved.
This so far there is little affect on my bottom half/legs. It does include an exercise chart with several options, which does include a lunge. I have not yet done the lunge.

Which brings me to: you must wear shoes!

My first time, as I took it out of the box and wanted to see, I was barefoot. Not smart. NOT that it caused pain.

But it didn’t feel great on the bottom of my feet as I pulled. The rubber band is a rubbery, hard tubing and it pulled on the bottom and was uncomfortable to stand and apply pressure on. I added the shoes and all was well.

Overall I think this is a great product and we are happy with it.

I will say there is a limit: it is Heavy Resistance and no way to interchange with others resistance levels. Other packages come with multiple resistance options. But if you are looking for a single weight, this does the trick.

We were also discussing how this would be great for travel. Again, with Covid, rather than worry about taking heavy hand weights or kettle bells or use a hotel’s workout space, this would be far easier and lighter. So that will be the plan for the future.

One Con: the handles are not the most comfortable. This is not enough to keep me from using the band. They are rough I’m sure in order to assure grip, but in future I’ll use weight gloves to get a better grip and counter the uncomfortable feeling of these.

Overall we are pleased with this Resistance Band and foresee continued successful use.

text_fidelity_a: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver) I'm not a serious prepper or anything, but I did live 5 days last February without power during the blizzard in Texas.  I have spent the subsequent months getting ready for another time like that again.  The video I watched was a cool way to heat an area in your house when the power is off.  I already had the rectangular paving stones/bricks to place on this table as well as the little alcohol burners.  The idea is to place the cement stones/bricks (the flat ones, not the large ones with holes in them) around the alcohol burner.  The alcohol burner transfers heat to the bricks which in turn release the stored heat over a longer time in the area where they are set up.  Obviously this can't be set up on the floor, so a table that can handle the stored heat is what I needed.  I set the cement blocks up on this metal camping table, put the alcohol burner in the middle and let it "work."  This camping table is the perfect size for my emergency room warming set up with the bricks an burner.  I know it will work fine for a table to use my propane cookstove on as well, but for the moment it is in an emergency box in my house along with the cement bricks and the alcohol burner (and a bottle of rubbing alcohol).  I'm very happy with how this table worked out for my purposes.
text_fidelity_b: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail The other reviews mentioning the finely threaded battery compartment are pretty accurate. The first thing I did when I got mine was wipe down the threads, there was definitely dust that immediately wiped off that I could see being a problem. After it was cleaned I applied a little bit of mineral oil to the threads (probably something better, but it is what I had), and the screwing/unscrewing was much smoother.

Once I added in the batteries and began screwing the cap back on, I could understand why so many people are worried about it. It is really hard to tell if the resistance you are feeling when screwing it back in is because of the spring on the cap, or because it is not threaded well. If you go carefully it should screw back on fine - especially if you clean the threads and apply a little oil.

The laser seems to function exactly as expected, the strobe mode blinks a little faster than I was expecting, but that is hardly a problem.

Will update once it gets some usage!

UPDATE (2 days later): Well the laser started acting weird... Randomly won't turn on, can't rack a shotgun more than a few times without it turning off - and I wasn't even shooting. I'm actually impressed by just how unreliable it is. Going to roll the dice and get an exchange, but my hopes are not very high at this point.

text_fidelity_a:
Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag I'm loving this reel. It replaced an Ambassadeur 5500C. The differences are pretty obvious. The Patriarch includes both a friction and magnetic breaking system. This might be a good thing if you have experience but it does take some time to get used to it. Nearest I can figure, the magnetic breaking is most effective at the beginning of the case where the speed is highest while the mechanical brake operates across the whole cast. When I change lures I usually turn up the magnetic to 8-10 and then adjust the mechanical until I clean casts. Then I back off the magnetic for the same result. The end result is nice long casts with fewer rats nests. Then - to add to the complication - you can pop off the side and adjust how many magnets are active in the magnetic breaking. I keep two on and four off (must be done in pairs). I get a few more yards (5 to 10 maybe) from the Patriarch compared with the 5500c.

Reeling back in is smooth. The moving eye lays the line smoothly on the spool but I notice that during casting the eye stays in one place. I can't remember for sure but I thought the 5500c eye moved during casts. Careful when you release the spool. The tension on the line may be enough to get the spools spinning and you can end up with a rats nest without even casting.

The Patriarch fits nicely in the palm while on the rod. It allows me to keep a finger on the spool and keep in touch with the line out the front. I have it mated to a St. Croix Legend Tournament Bass Casting Rod and I think the combination is perfect though I'd like to try it out with a slightly lighter and slower action rod. I'll bet it can shoot a 1/2 ounce lure a half mile!

I didn't like my dealings with support. As I mentioned, you can engage or disengage magnets in the break system but I couldn't figure out how. The minimal instruction pamphlet didn't give any clues and neither did their support website. In fact, looking through some forums I'm guessing most people find access to the magnets obvious. But I didn't know how to do it and support responded with "Unfortunately, to experiment with the centrifugal breaks, you must take
the reel apart to access them." Wow. Helpful guys. Maybe I lost something in the translation. I don't know. Fortunately for me I feel the reel is so well built I'll never have to contact support so I'll just ignore them.

You can fish well with any nice baitcaster. This isn't going to put bigger or more fish on your hook. But you'll find each cast is a pleasure.
text_fidelity_b: Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag

text_fidelity_a:
Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft I have zero business affiliation with amazon or Shrade. I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft

text_fidelity_a:
Whatafit Resistance Bands Set, Exercise Bands with Door Anchor, Handles, Carry Bag, Legs Ankle Straps for Resistance Training, Physical Therapy, Home Workouts I wanted to wait until I had some time to use these and now I can say that I am so happy I bought these back in March. If you're stuck at home and need to workout these are great. The bands are versatile that you can workout almost every major muscle group you'd hit at the gym. I was a little concerned that after 2-3 months of daily use the bands would snap or be stretched out too much but so far they're still working great. And really resistance wise you can combine bands to increase resistance enough that you can feel like you've gotten a good pump. It takes a bit getting used to if you miss your freeweights or machines but after months of home workouts I have to admit I've gotten great results maintaining my gains from the gym.

From opening the box, you get a lot for your money; this is a great value and a godsend for those who are out of the gym and have to rely on homeworkouts. My only complaint is the door anchor can make certain workouts awkward, but that's really just down to whatever kind of doors you have in your home. Depending on our set up you may want to get 2 anchors or maybe one of those anchors that wrap around the whole door and have multiple loops and anchor points but that's really just up to you.

Overall this a great product and I would recommend it as an investment for homeworkouts. I don't know how I would have survived quarantine this long without them.

Update: I wanted to provide some more information. After 6 months of almost daily use, one the bands finally snapped. Obviously not a big deal; I certainly was happy and got my money's worth. The bands were certainly durable and allowed me to stay in shape. I was ready to buy a new replacement set but I asked Whatafit if by some chance there was some warranty on the band. They sent me a whole replacement set! No problem no fighting, just sent them a pic of the broken band and they were on it. I can't say enough how good this product and this company is. I have totally changed my opinion on the value of bands for working out and I would definitely buy from this company. 5 stars .

OutSmart Gear 3 in 1 Ultralight Titanium Spork | Portable and Reusable Multi Tool for Backpacking and Camping | Feed Your Face, Leave No Trace I really wanted to love this. I still love the idea, but the execution isn't quite there. The light weight is amazing. Titanium is legit. The combination of a spoon on one end and a fork sounds like a winner, as you forego the compromises of a spork. Sadly for some reason neither the fork nor the spoon are great. The fork is oddly wide, which we'll get to later. Likewise the spoon isn't too deep. Neither the fork nor the spoon are ideal.

I might have still someone gave this 5 stars (titanium is that cool!), but alas there's the serrated edge. It's not really useful, and when combined with the wide fork, it means you'll be tearing at you gums unless you have a huge mouth. That's kinda a dealbreaker. I could see past the other issues in a camping/backpacking context, but tearing your gums just isn't fun!

Still gave it 4 stars if you have a big (or at least wide) mouth.

text_fidelity_a:
GoSports Synthetic Corn Fill, 8 Pound Bulk Bag - Great for Cornhole Bags, Crafts and More, Yellow My use for this may be a bit unusual. I have an adjustable Indian club and needed something to put inside as a weight. I wanted something that would allow me to break the weight down into at least 0.25 pound increments but not so fine that I'd be sweeping up little bits of it every time I cleaned my floors (because, sooner or later, no matter how careful I am, I'm going to drop and scatter some of it). The material also needed to stand up to being thrown around inside the body of the club as I swung .

This stuff is perfect. It's large enough to easily find when I drop it but small enough to weigh out exactly in whatever increment I work. I weighed it out into 0.5 pound increments and put those into sandwich bags to make changing weights more efficient. Then I started a 21-day training program that required 100 swings per day. The bags needed replacing periodically -- which is understandable as that's definitely not what they were designed for -- but the pellets still look new. I should also note that I did not get 8 pounds as advertised; I got just over 8 pounds and 10 ounces.

I had no idea that plastic corn pellets were a thing until I started searching for filler for my club, but I'm very glad I found this. What I have now will keep me going for a while, but when I'm ready to up the weight, I'll definitely buy another box of this.
text_fidelity_b: GoSports Synthetic Corn Fill, 8 Pound Bulk Bag - Great for Cornhole Bags, Crafts and More, Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Gerber Answer FAST Knife, Serrated Edge [22-41970] Well, first off this is my first assisted opening knife, so operationally it was new to me flicking it out. Anyway, about the knife, it is a very well made. I have no problems with the quality of the construction of the knife.

But, how would it work for self defense situations? I carried it this weekend to see how easy it would be to get to it in a quick deployment situation. What I found is that the clip was to tight and it would be difficult to get off of my pocket. ok, no big deal, pair of needle nose pliers and it is looser. But what I noticed beyond that was that the single button used for locking and releasing the blade can cause deployment problems. Wanting to show off my new knife to a buddy of mine, I pulled it out of my pocket and tried to flip the blade. Damn, it was locked, good thing it wasn't a bad guy. What I found is that when you put the blade in your pocket, or when you reach for it, there is a very very good chance you have put the button in the lock position. So when you pull it out to deploy if it is locked, it is locked and you have to unlock it before flicking it out. Unfortunately you cannot disable this feature because this button also serves to lock the blade out and releases the blade for folding. So, unless you can train yourself in a very stressful self def situation to use fine motor skills to unlock a button, I wouldn't use it in that capacity.

So bottom line, good knife, but wouldn't use it for self defense purposes. I'll keep carrying my other non assisted opening Gerber knife for self defense.
text_fidelity_b: Gerber Answer FAST Knife, Serrated Edge [22-41970]

text_fidelity_a: Lightspeed Outdoors Sun Shelter Tent | Durable Beach Tent Sun Shelter with Clip-Up Privacy Feature | Beach Tent Pop Up with Side-Pull Hub System for Quick Set Up | Fits 3-4 Adults | Hibiscus This is perhaps my husband's only purchase ever that he has made on behalf of our child. I had zero involvement and I was happy to let go of one of "my chores". I approved of the fact that he did his research. Research for me involves countless hours weighing options on the internet, reading reviews, analyzing cost, looking for coupons or discounts, and finally leaving it and a few other finalists to sit in cart limbo for a week or more while I wait for the clear choice to present itself to me in a dream. Research for him involved eyeing a few samples he liked on the beach, talking to the owners about their thoughts, taking a few pictures and then finding the right one online and clicking "add to cart" in One. Single. Day. The tent came quickly. Arrived on time. I picked it up from the post office and was already judgemental and catty about how much the box weighed. Sigh. Why am I like this? Overall the tent is good. We needed something for our 2-year-old son to nap in on the beach so we don't have to pack up and leave at 11:30 everytime. It's time, after all, that we try to reclaim some semblance of our own lives. For this purpose it has worked 3 times. It's too big for our needs but that's not really a complaint and it is a bit heavy but my husband has taken ownership over the whole thing and insists on carrying it himself. He's the only one who has ever assembled or disassembled the thing and he insists it's easy. It seems a bit tall for me to assemble on my own. I wanted it to be the kind that just pops up and folds flat but he liked this one because it had vents. Vents are infinitely more important because it gets hot as a mofo inside when in the direct sunlight and if you can't catch a breeze. I thought the fold up part that stretches to the outside and acts as a sort of patio was stupid at first because who wants to sit or walk on that texture fabric at the beach but it occludes the view of people doing way more fun things than sleeping and for that reason it is essential. It lost a star because of the weight and because one of the loops that secures one of the windows has torn off already and I can foresee it happening again.
text_fidelity_b: Lightspeed Outdoors Sun Shelter Tent | Durable Beach Tent Sun Shelter with Clip-Up Privacy Feature | Beach Tent Pop Up with Side-Pull Hub System for Quick Set Up | Fits 3-4 Adults | Hibiscus

text_fidelity_a:
TurboFire DVD Workout I purchased TurboJam and went from a size 18 to a 12 in five months in 2006. I'm currently a size 16 and have been stuck since 2008 after the birth of my son 4 years ago. TurboJam was just boring and after seeing my long lost friend Chalene on an infomercial advertising this product I was excited to try this. I quit smoking on March 23, ditch the wine and laced up my shoes and got busy. The choreography is difficult. The Fire Starter class took me two weeks to learn. (May take you less, I was struggling to quit smoking while learning this).Thank God some of these moves I learned from TurboJam or I would have given up.
I tried the new to class option and its not cued well and it takes forever to work off the clock. I'm a college student and busy mom and the New Class option can take longer. Every DVD the choreography is different and I hate that aspect as well. I just want to do the workout and get on with my day. I decided to learn all the moves on the cardio DVDs first before I add the HIIT, Core, Sculpt, Abs. You don't have to learn any moves for these, they are cued workouts. The only thing I don't like is the "fake" spray tanned women in the video because its misleading. Spray tans bring out the best on your body and make you look lean, sculpted, and thinner. I was disappointed Chalene allowed that.
I think the positive I've gotten out of the video is I'm approaching day 60, and I went from 240 to 220. I'm still a size 16, but the results are real and noticeable. Im almost in a size 14 and I'm excited about my 90 days being up in June 2013. I will do another 90 days of TurboFire, which will be a total of 180 days. I will then incorporate ChaLean Xtreme Hybrid Program.
I think if you are tired of being fat and overweight you can achieve anything. Just keep pushing play and don't give up. Also I don't count calories I just picked a few meals from breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and eat them and use portion control. Good Luck.

text_fidelity_a:
JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds A great product. Last winter we lost a much beloved trampoline to extreme winds. I set out on a search for a product that could prevent the loss of the replacement trampoline. I found a number of products on various websites that could best be described as variations on a tent stake design. They offered stakes that were straight or U shaped, and I was very nervous that in a windy situation (especially with rain softened ground), that the stakes would just pull free. I was about to fashion my own solution using spiral dog stakes when I found this kit.

Suffice it to say that the components are sturdy and well made. They are packaged well, and the instructions are clear and easy to follow. However, what makes this a five star product is that it contains everything you need to create a stable tie down for a trampoline, and it contains enough anchors to tie it down for wind from any direction. The anchors are not trivial to "screw" into the ground. I did it on a day after heavy rains and still required a tool for leverage. This was reassuring, because it meant that they would hold fast when the ground dried, and would allow the straps to transfer load from the trampoline frame to the stakes and the ground effectively.

I was very pleased with the product, and would heartily recommend it.

UPDATE: This stakedown kit works very well. Since installing, we have had four windstorms with gusts over 20 mph, and the trampoline has stayed perfectly in place. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds

text_fidelity_a:
Sportline 885 Flip Pack Hydration Waist Pack I had to submit my review after reading the other ones that didn't rate it so high. I have not had the same issues with my pack. It's exactly what I've been looking for. I've been running for two years and had previously used a standard pack that has one water bottle that sat right in the small of my back. However, I had been looking for away to attach my iPhone to it safely since I couldn't stand using an arm band.

I was so excited when I saw this pack in the store. It was just what I had been wanting. However, although it has the perfect holder for an iPhone, I was a little reluctant to purchase this at first because I was 1.) worried that it would be awkward running with a pack in the front; 2.) worried that the velcro would not be enough to keep the phone velcroed down and from flopping around....also the normal wear and tear on the velcro from flipping up the phone to note my pace on my RunKeeper app.

Admittedly, the pack doesn't work so well in the direct front as a runner...would probably be okay for a walker. However, there is too much bounce to allow that to be comfortable. It did much better when I moved it around to the back...however, it defeated the purpose of being able to monitor my pace as I was running.

I finally figured out that if I put it on my right side with the bottle toward the back part, that I could accomplish everything I needed. iPhone and app are easily accessible..in fact, I rarely need to flip up the phone to see my pace. I can usually see it by barely tipping it up. The water bottle is still handy and I'm able to use my arms without smacking it.

So, while I'm not strictly using it as designed, it suits my purpose just like I needed. I'm really happy with it. Some other things:

1.) The belt isn't that big. If your waist size is 40 inches plus, you might have a tough time getting it to snap.
2.) The water bottle holder is great. My old holder was all material. I like the reinforced strips that make it stiff enough to jam the bottle back in...yet is lightweight and holds the bottle tightly.
3. Water bottle is pretty standard...just right.
4.) The zippered pouch is bigger than I orginally thought. Holds spare key, chapstick, Gu and $ just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Sportline 885 Flip Pack Hydration Waist Pack

NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16

text_fidelity_a:
Sunlite Rear Wire Folding Basket I live on my boat in Los Angeles. I am within a 10 minute bike ride to several grocery stores and wanted to use my bike for as much shopping as possible. The trip by bike is shorter (timewise) that using my car, parking is much easier, and closer to the stores and faster. Sometimes searching for a parking place takes longer than driving to the store.

I mention my location because weather did not factor into my decision grid when selecting cargo carriers on my bike. If I still lived in Seattle I probably would have gone for a rainproof option.

So when I bought my bike I immediately bought a Wald folding basket to attach to my rear rack. The design has several shortcomings but I was able to get it installed using wire ties, rather than the metal clips Wald provided, and it has served my purposes. The mounting hardware Wald provided did not fit the rack on my bike and was not the same color as the basket and my bike. .

When I decided to add a second basket to the other side of the rear rack on my bike I decided to try the Sunlite model because it had a few features I now knew would be valuable (experience with the Wald basket taught me a lot and made me appreciate the reviewer's comments on both products).

Here are the main reasons that I find the Sunlite product to be superior to the wald basket. I have uploaded three photographs that address my reasons for preferring the Sunlite product. The Sunlite basket is on the left on my bike and the Wald one is on the right.

1. The sunlite model is larger when open which benefits cargo capacity.

2. Sunlite thought out the attachment options better and even provided some beefy wire ties as an attachment option. I did not use the provided hose clamps because I thought they would scratch my bike and the black wire ties matched my bike. Sunlite provided a couple of really beefy wire ties but I had to use some of my own to finish the job. More wire ties would be nice.

3. The latch that keeps the sunlite basket closed is much more effective that the one on the Wald. One of the photos I uploaded shows the bungee cord work around I use to keep my wald basket closed when its not in use. In the photo you can see the damage to the finish on the wald basket that was a result of the latch scratching the paint. In the long run the Sunlite latch might not be any better but its starting out as way more effective that the one on the Wald Basket. One of the problems with the Wald latch is that it seems to have been designed for an unpainted basket and the layers of paint on the latch and basked wire makes the latch very difficult to rotate.

4. The mesh bottom on the Sunlite basket keeps my mail from falling through the bottom of the basket. That is a problem with the wald basket when I stop by our mailbox on the same trip to the grocery store.

5, The finish on the Sunlite basket is better than the one on the wald basket.

Both of these baskets handle quite a bit of weight with no problem. I have put three 12 packs of soda in my Wald basket and it has held them secure.

Reviewers for both products have mentioned the fact that you need to bend the outer wall of the basket outward to get the support for the bottom in place. This is mentioned as a disadvantage but I look at that as a feature that assures me that the bottom wont fall out of my basket when Im using it.

The Wald basket is slightly cheaper than the Sunlite but, in my opinion, it is not enough cheaper to justify the Wald over the Sunlite. On the other hand the Wald basket is serviceable enough that I'm not going to replace it with a second Sunlite.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Rear Wire Folding Basket

text_fidelity_a: Seaflo 12V DC 1.2 GPM 35 PSI 21-Series Diaphragm Water Pressure Pump for Caravan/RV/Boat/Marine Got this to pump water out of a 55 gal barrel using a 12v battery charged by 45 watt solar panel.  Didn't know the inlet/outlet openings were only 1/4" but fortunately I had a 3/4" garden hose reducer with a 1/4" opening at the opposite end.  I connected 1/4" tubing to the pump.  Put one end of the tubing (connected to inlet side) up over the barrel into the water, & pushed the 1/4" outlet tubing (side with arrow pointing out) into the reducer which was screwed onto a 40 ft garden hose which was stretched out uphill.  I wasn't sure this small pump would move water uphill from a 55 gal barrel for that distance, but after several minutes, water started trickling out of the garden hose onto one of the bushes I wanted watered.  The trickle was just right to have it soak in as I did other chores then came back to move the hose to the next bush.  The arrow on the pump that shows which way the water should flow thru the pump is kind of hard to see, so turn the pump at different angles to the light until you see it.

The cloth covers for the rear saddles make sliding your kayak up easy and the straps, guylines and hooks are good quality. I used this product when I picked up my new fishing kayak and drove 90 miles with it home.

Now to the "for some kayaks" part. The saddles pivot and fold in or out to adjust to various kayak hull diameters. For a traditional kayak or canoe hull this would work really well and automatically center the boat in the saddles. However I have a Wilderness Systems Radar 135 fishing kayak. The hull is a fairly complex shape with the sides being almost square and continuing underneath into a pontoon section on both sides and a fairly flat bottom in the middle. The prow is pointed like a normal, but flattens out after about 2 feet. All these weird shapes combine to make it difficult to center the boat on the saddles and trying to adjust the boat once on the saddles is difficult. Will be looking for an alternative rack.

It's a good product, unfortunately it just won't work very well for the type of kayak I have. Anybody in the market for a used once kayak rack? :P

text_fidelity_a:
Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177) Back in 1977 I purchased one of the first models of this pistol, and used it for years. Around 2003 I lost it. Long story short I loaned it to someone and never got it back. Guessing you know the moral to that story.

Just recently I've gotten the urge to do some target shooting in my back yard - I can probably blame watching episodes of [[ASIN:B003NX6C1C Top Shot]] for that. So I wanted to replace my 1377, mainly because I still had all the accessories for it. So I got on Amazon and found this one to purchase.

To be honest, I did not read the information on the product page - just ordered it. A few days later I had the pistol in my hands. First thing I noticed is it's not quite the gun I remember having. Apparently the design has been changed. Gone was the pull knob that you used to cock the gun and instead there is a breach mechanism. I think I actually like the new design better.

One of the biggest surprise for me was that this model no longer makes use of Bbs. Gone is the magnetic tip on the end of loading pin. Wish I had know that before including this package in my order - [[ASIN:B000HKKY7M Crosman Copperhead 6000 Copper Coated BBs in a Bottle]]. But, that is my fault for not paying attention to what was on the product page.

Anyway - even just shooting pellets I am having fun with this gun. I also bought packs of these pellets - [[ASIN:B001DCB61Q Crosman Destroyer .177 Cal, 7.9 Grains, Pointed, 250ct]] & [[ASIN:B002DM0ZIU Crosman Hollow Point Pellets, 0.177-Calibre]]. Both seem to work well.

I've been having a lot of fun plinking cans and shooting targets. I think this pellet gun is great.
text_fidelity_b: Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177)

text_fidelity_a:
Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue) I grabbed this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair with a thought towards our days at the beach. Sometimes we have chairs, sometimes just the towels, but I thought this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair might offer me a nice, supportive place to sit. My wife tends to lay out for sun, but I like watching the water and thinking... but I can get tired and start to hurt on the hard sand. This is smaller and easier to carry overall (I thought), so why not. In the end, I think I’m going to be correct in my assessment. We’re not getting back out there (yet), but the time is soon upon us for our beach days and I can’t wait.

The Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair is a cool idea - a stadium seat type set up: flips open, cushion, back support. I’ve tried one or two such seats and thought, eh. But we don’t do stadiums enough. We do, however, sit on the floor from time to time, go to the beach, mediate, and so forth. Hitting that “middle age” timeframe, my wife and I would love to have something more comfortable.

1. I gave it 5 stars because overall it feels like that’s right for comfort, ease of use, and so forth. I would consider a 4 star for the magnets that hold the seat to the frame. I’ve had the seat cushions pop off every time I’ve picked it up to carry/move, or take pictures. My wife has not as such luck, only having them fall a couple time. Closed they’d slide up coming off for me, so I’d be worried about loosing one or two or all three - though I’m sure one would notice that many.

2. The cushions are nice for comfort. It comes with three, with one having a strap on the back to hold it onto the other - so you can have a double seat cushion, which is a nice add on.

3. Seems to hold a good amount of weight. I’ve got some extra pounds on right now and it seems to handle me well. I’m taking it off, so hoping it won’t be there all summer as I plan to use it, but so far, so good.

4. The frame seems solid and like it’ll hold up. Again, it holds our weight (individually) and allows us to feel well supported. My wife has tried it more, sitting both cross legged and straight and feels like she can sit there for a good amount of time in both positions.

5. The seat cushions are good - not too thick (though thicker is always better), but not too thin. They were comfortable on both the back and seat.

6. This Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair comes with a strap that you can remove, attaching to the base of the frame allowing you to carry it over the shoulder. My wife did this and felt like both the strap was comfortable, while the chair was not too heavy. We both agree this is a solid, with a noticeable weight to it, but nothing most folks couldn’t handle (we think), finding the strap to be a good addition to aiding that. This is where you’ll want to be aware of the magnets not necessarily holding the seat in place - at least one popped off each time I tried, but only once for my wife. Because of how it sets when you are carrying on the strap - with the open side downward - it would allow the cushion to slip out onto the ground. I grabbed it before it did, but one needs to be aware, so as not to loose any. We talked about adding a strap of our own (sort of a bungie type thing) to hold the cushions in place. But that could be used for other things as well - we just don’t know what that is at this point.

7. Back support - we have only used it on the bed (that was not working too well as we’d fall over, but it was fun trying) and floor in the living room. But the back support was solid and let us feel comfortable. We both felt like it would be a nice support and keep us from hunching over and getting sore quickly.

In the end we are both impressed with this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair and plan to get some solid use out of it. I think this will be one item where time will tell - does it hold up, does it allow for longer periods of sitting, does it take different surfaces (beach, floor, grass, etc)? We’re happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue)
